items.name: Humain
items.why: This week HUMAIN announced AMD AI-in-a-Box for Saudi enterprise adoption, an 84MW NVIDIA AI-factory expansion, and a NEOM giga campus with Nebius as first tenant—clear, multi-front infra scale-up. Not in Salesforce; sovereign model-serving demand is imminent as capacity comes online.
items.message: Congrats on the AMD AI-in-a-Box launch and the NVIDIA / NEOM campus buildout—moving from factory MW to enterprise tenants in the same week is a rare scale moment. As ALLaM and packaged enterprise AI land on that GPU-agnostic stack, inference cost and latency will dominate unit economics for both HUMAIN and campus customers. Modular’s MAX engine is built for high-throughput, portable serving across GPU vendors without rewriting runtimes. Would you be open to a 30-minute working session next week with your AI platform leads to map MAX against one production or pilot workload on the new capacity?

items.name: ElevenLabs
items.why: Instant Soundtrack launched today (video→music/SFX in one pass), on top of a planned hundreds-of-millions India investment and public margin/IPO focus—direct pressure on real-time multimodal inference cost. New logo, not in SF.
items.message: Saw the Instant Soundtrack launch—analyzing video and generating music and SFX in a single pass is a meaningful step-up in multimodal serving load versus character/audio-minute voice alone. Combined with the India capacity build and the margin conversation around IPO timing, inference efficiency looks board-relevant. Modular’s MAX stack helps teams cut latency and $/generated-minute on production voice and audio pipelines without locking to a single cloud. Happy to share how similar generative-audio teams structure serving for bursty creative traffic—open to a short call this week with whoever owns inference cost for new product surfaces?

items.name: OpenEvidence
items.why: OneOncology partnership (Oct 25) embeds clinical AI in physician workflows right after FT’s ~$15bn growth profile, Johns Hopkins collaboration, and a settled Doximity dispute—distribution and usage are about to spike. Not in SF; Baseten-served fine-tuned LLM volume is a direct Modular wedge.
items.message: The OneOncology partnership to put OpenEvidence inside clinical workflows, alongside the Johns Hopkins collaboration, points to a sharp rise in low-latency, high-reliability inference for clinicians. At the volumes implied by the FT coverage—and with the Doximity matter settled—serving cost and SLA consistency become as important as model quality. Modular’s MAX inference engine is designed for dense, fine-tuned LLM traffic with predictable latency and better GPU utilization. Would your eng/infra leads have 25 minutes this week to walk through how you’re scaling weekly custom-model calls and where a MAX proof-of-concept could reduce cost without touching clinical UX?

items.name: Krea
items.why: Krea 3 launched this week for commercial teams, with Krea 3 Ultra ranking top-five and messaging faster/cheaper edits than GPT Image 2.5—speed and unit economics are the product pitch. Not in SF; Together-served image/video gen maps cleanly to MAX.
items.message: Congratulations on Krea 3 for commercial teams and the early ranking for Krea 3 Ultra—especially the framing around faster, lower-cost edits versus frontier image models. Interactive editing only stays differentiated if inference stays cheap under concurrent creative-team load. Modular builds MAX specifically for that problem: higher throughput and lower latency on image/video generation workloads so product claims hold as usage scales. If useful, we could run a short benchmark against one of your production editing paths and compare cost-per-edit and p95 latency—would next week work for a technical intro with the serving owners?

items.name: HeyGen
items.why: HeyGen’s first general-purpose video model topped Artificial Analysis’ silent T2V leaderboard (Oct 24), on the heels of high-profile avatar partnerships—clear step-function in generative-video inference demand. Not in SF.
items.message: Impressive milestone with the general-purpose video model topping the Artificial Analysis silent text-to-video leaderboard—especially alongside scaled avatar deployments like the Serhant content engine. Leaderboard wins tend to translate quickly into production traffic, which is where video-gen serving cost and queue latency usually bite. Modular’s MAX engine helps teams serve generative video and avatar pipelines with better GPU efficiency and more predictable latency under burst load. Open to a focused conversation this week with your ML infra team on where serving is the constraint as the new model rolls out?

items.name: SK Telecom
items.why: Bloomberg (Oct 23): SK’s data-center arm in talks to help fund a ~$350B AI buildout, plus SKT’s first AI governance report this week—sovereign telco AI at hyperscale with Together-class serving already in the mix. Not in SF.
items.message: The reported talks around financing a ~$350B AI infrastructure buildout, paired with SK Telecom’s first AI governance report, suggest you’re formalizing how A. and telco agents will run in production at national scale. That usually surfaces two constraints at once: inference economics across large GPU fleets, and a stack that fits enterprise/telco compliance. Modular’s MAX inference engine is built for high-throughput, production-grade serving with clear operational controls. I’d welcome 30 minutes with the AI platform or cloud leadership this week to discuss how MAX could sit in the SK AI stack as capacity expands.

items.name: Salesforce
items.why: $5.7B Braze deal coverage landed today—marketing automation + Agentforce agentic CRM implies heavier multi-model inference as stacks integrate. Named Together customer; not in Modular’s SF.
items.message: Coverage of the Braze acquisition puts a clear marker on deepening marketing and engagement automation inside the Salesforce AI ecosystem—on top of Agentforce’s agentic CRM workloads. Integration periods are when inference volume and latency SLAs get re-architected, often before cost is locked in. Modular’s MAX engine helps platforms run multi-model agent and personalization traffic more efficiently without rewriting application layers. If your Agentforce or AI infra teams are sizing post-Braze serving, I’d like to offer a short technical briefing this week on latency and cost profiles we’ve seen for similar agent stacks.

items.name: LMArena
items.why: $200M Series B at $3.1B (Oct 13) to advance AI evaluation—fresh capital into leaderboard/eval infra that burns continuous multi-model inference. Net-new, not in SF, no incumbent competitor lock confirmed.
items.message: Congrats on the $200M Series B at $3.1B—scaling an evaluation arena means sustained, bursty multi-model serving across open and frontier endpoints, which is one of the harder inference cost profiles to keep flat. Modular’s MAX stack is designed for high-concurrency model serving with strong throughput-per-GPU, which tends to matter when leaderboard and eval traffic spike. We’re working with teams that run similar multi-model fleets and can share patterns that cut serving cost without slowing eval turnaround. Would you or your infra lead have time this week for a concrete discussion on current serving bottlenecks?

items.name: EliseAI
items.why: a16z/Bessemer-led raise to ~$4B (late Sept) plus mid-October RealPage integration pause keeps EliseAI in a capital-rich, platform-rebuild window—conversational/voice AI on Baseten is a direct serving conversation. Not in SF.
items.message: The path to a ~$4B valuation and the public RealPage integration pause together suggest a moment where EliseAI may re-platform or harden how tenant- and health-facing conversational AI is served. Property and healthcare voice agents are latency-sensitive and usage-spiky; serving cost compounds quickly as coverage expands. Modular’s MAX inference engine is built for production LLM and voice agent traffic with better utilization and clearer latency control. Happy to compare notes this week with your eng leadership on inference architecture as you scale past the current partner footprint.

items.name: Moonshot AI
items.why: Kimi K3.1 Pro (~3T params) launched this week and Reuters reports subscriber quota resets after launch issues—concrete serving/capacity strain. Already a Partner, but the reliability signal is exceptional for Modular this week.
items.message: The Kimi K3.1 Pro launch—and the subsequent quota adjustments after rollout strain—is a familiar pattern at multi-trillion-parameter scale: demand outruns serving headroom before the product narrative cools. Modular’s MAX engine focuses on exactly that gap—higher tokens-per-GPU and more stable latency under launch traffic for frontier open-weight models. Given our existing partnership path, a useful next step would be a joint look at the K3.1 Pro serving path where quotas tightened. Can we schedule a working session this week with the serving owners to identify one concrete optimization target?

items.name: Black Forest Labs
items.why: FLUX 3 Image Klein open weights (consumer 8GB VRAM, SMB commercial use) plus Fal’s FLUX 3 Max video post-train mid-October—self-host and partner-hosted gen demand both rising. SF Prospect; Together exclusivity makes a timely alternative-serving conversation.
items.message: Opening FLUX 3 Image Klein weights for smaller commercial users—and the Fal FLUX 3 Max video collaboration—will pull a lot of self-hosted and partner-hosted generation onto diverse GPUs. That distribution is powerful, but it usually surfaces a second problem: keeping latency and cost competitive as third parties scale FLUX traffic. Modular’s MAX stack is a strong fit for optimized image/video serving across commodity and datacenter GPUs without forcing a single host platform. As a next step, I’d like 30 minutes with your partnerships or infra team this week to explore a MAX-backed serving path alongside existing launch partners.

items.message: Your write-up on the knowledge fabric for enterprise agents, together with the hire to lead sovereign-AI sales, reads like Sarvam is moving squarely into production agent workloads—where grounding quality and serving economics both have to work. Indic multimodal and voice agents at aggressive token pricing only hold if inference efficiency is exceptional on the current GPU allocation. Modular’s MAX engine is built to raise throughput and cut serving cost for sovereign LLM/voice stacks without changing the developer-facing API. Jay’s already on the account—happy to join a working session this week on one enterprise-agent serving path and a concrete MAX evaluation plan.
